stem: Before crushing a solid oral medication for administration through an enteral feeding tube, what should the nurse verify first?

options.A: Whether the specific dosage form is suitable for manipulation and tube administration; some modified-release and enteric-coated products should not be crushed.
options.B: Whether the tablet is physically large, because formulation design does not affect the safety of crushing it for tube administration.
options.C: Whether enteral nutrition is infusing, because every solid oral medication becomes safe to crush while tube feeding is running.
options.D: Whether the client can taste the medication, because taste determines whether a tablet can be safely crushed for tube administration.

rationale: Before a solid dosage form is manipulated for enteral-tube administration, the nurse must determine whether that specific product is suitable for crushing or other manipulation. Evidence and enteral-medication guidance identify modified-release and enteric-coated dosage forms as common examples that may be inappropriate to crush, and inappropriate manipulation can alter drug delivery or contribute to tube problems. Tablet size, taste, or the mere presence of running nutrition does not establish that a dosage form is safe to crush.
educational_objective: Verify the suitability of the exact oral dosage form before crushing a medication for enteral-tube administration, with special attention to modified-release and enteric-coated products.
source_organization: American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (ASPEN), Journal of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
source_document_title: Developing guidance for feeding tube administration of oral medications
source_locator: Abstract — Methods/Results/Conclusion on evaluating oral medications for safe feeding-tube administration; article guidance/table assessing dosage-form suitability; references to noncrushable modified-release/enteric-coated products
source_claim_supported: Medication dosage forms must be evaluated for suitability before manipulation for feeding-tube administration; some oral products are inappropriate for crushing/tube delivery.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed p.12, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — evaluate appropriateness and accuracy of medication orders; prepare and administer medications using rights of medication administration; review pertinent data before medication administration
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication preparation for enteral feeding tubes

source_original.stem: Before crushing a tablet for administration through an enteral feeding tube, what should the nurse verify?

options.A: Whether the dosage form can be safely manipulated; modified-release and enteric-coated products may not be crushable
options.B: Whether the tablet is large enough to crush; formulation design does not affect tube-administration safety
options.C: Whether tube feeding is running, because all solid oral medications are safe to crush when nutrition is infusing
options.D: Whether the client can taste the medicine, because taste determines whether a tablet can be crushed safely

source_original.rationale: Medication suitability must be checked before crushing for tube administration. Modified-release and enteric-coated products are common examples that may be inappropriate to crush because manipulation can alter release, efficacy, safety, or tube patency.
source_original.source_detail: JPEN 2023, PMID 36847617: evaluation of oral dosage forms for feeding-tube administration and appropriateness of crushing/manipulation; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Kept the dosage-form safety construct but corrected the blueprint from Safety/Infection to Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, narrowed unsupported mechanism claims, strengthened the exact verify-first wording, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: ASPEN/JPEN feeding-tube medication study/guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: 2023 guidance remains directly relevant; 2026 literature continues to characterize modified-release and enteric-coated formulations as inappropriate to manipulate without suitability review.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The source directly supports evaluating each oral product for feeding-tube suitability before crushing/manipulation.

distractor_audit.A: Correct; addresses the required dosage-form suitability check.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; formulation design is central to whether manipulation is appropriate.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; tube feeding does not make all solid formulations safe to crush.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; taste does not determine dosage-form manipulation safety.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A describes the prerequisite medication-safety assessment.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives answer what should be verified before crushing; no second correct check is presented.
audit_findings.blueprint: Corrected to NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12, because the construct is medication preparation/administration rather than general environmental safety.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-solved the final item, rechecked the 2023 ASPEN/JPEN source and NCSBN p.12, challenged category placement and the wording 'may not be crushable,' and confirmed A remained uniquely correct.
